name: options-for-a-vector-store
query: We need a vector store for about two million chunks and we're OSS-only. What are my options?
why: The canonical options question. The skill surveys the retrieval layer of the bundled map with the OSS framing before recommending one path, and nothing is being built yet.

name: is-it-still-maintained
query: Is LangGraph still actively maintained, or has that project gone quiet?
why: A maintenance-status question asked to inform a decision. Answered from the dated corpus with its as-of date, never from training memory.

name: what-does-this-license-oblige
query: If we ship a commercial product on top of that AGPL vector database, what does the license actually oblige us to do?
why: License judgment on a catalogued component. License traps are one of the four things this skill owns, and the answer comes from the corpus row, not recall.

name: review-a-proposed-architecture
query: Here's the design for our support copilot: every user turn re-embeds the whole conversation and fans out to three separate indexes. Does that hold up?
why: Architecture review against the engineering principles. No new components are being chosen and no repo is being generated, so it stays on the read path.

name: what-does-this-tool-buy-me
query: What does a dedicated agent memory framework actually give me over writing conversation summaries to Postgres myself?
why: Component judgment - what a tool is for, what it costs to adopt, where it breaks. The honest answer may be that the simpler path wins.

name: orienting-with-no-project
query: What's the current state of open-source agent harnesses? I don't have a project yet, I'm just orienting.
why: Currency plus options with build intent explicitly disclaimed. The contrast case that keeps the scaffold skill from absorbing every AI question.

name: build-me-an-agent
query: Build me an agent that triages our inbound support email and drafts replies.
why: Belongs to ai-agent-project-scaffold. Any build-me-an-agent request goes through intake there, even if intake concludes a plain script suffices.

name: add-ai-to-an-existing-app
query: We have a Django app already. Add a chat assistant to it that answers from our help center articles.
why: Belongs to ai-agent-project-scaffold, which explicitly covers adding an AI subsystem to an existing repo. Advising on components stays here; building one does not.

name: stack-for-a-committed-build
query: We've committed to building a document-extraction service this quarter. Which stack should we use?
why: Belongs to ai-agent-project-scaffold. The hardest case on this seam: it reads like an options question, but there is a specific system being built, so it needs intake and a committed stack with every slot filled.

name: record-what-broke
query: Note that Chroma fell over above fifty thousand documents for us on the 0.5 line. I want that written down.
why: Belongs to ai-engineering-update, which owns field notes and every data file under resources/.

name: refresh-the-catalog
query: Refresh the AI tooling catalog - I think a chunk of those entries is a year out of date.
why: Belongs to ai-engineering-update. This skill reads the corpus; the update skill is the only write path into it.

name: research-a-tool-from-scratch
query: Research the state of open-weight embedding models thoroughly and come back with sources and dates.
why: Belongs to deep-research. The subject is AI tooling, but the request is for multi-angle verified web research, which this skill delegates rather than performs; folding the result in afterward goes to ai-engineering-update.

name: concurrency-bug-with-an-llm-in-it
query: Our FastAPI endpoint that calls the LLM times out under load. How do I fix the concurrency?
why: General software engineering with an AI label on it, so it routes to agent-skills. No component is being chosen and no tooling claim is in question.

name: write-an-mcp-server
query: Write an MCP server that exposes our internal ticketing API.
why: Belongs to build-mcp-server. This skill can say which MCP servers fit a stack, but MCP scaffolding is never hand-rolled here.
